answer: An agent market can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable credential issued after a costly real-world verification, then slash that bond when independently audited jobs show fraud. A whisper of planted fake reviews may sway one buyer, but repeated identities cannot cheaply multiply votes or reputation: each new persona needs another verified credential and locked stake. Like basalt on an island, the barrier is not impossible to cross; it makes a Sybil campaign costly and exposes the attacker to measurable losses.
